name: Adikesava Perumal Temple, Mylapore
deity: Adi Kesava Perumal (Vishnu), with Mayuravalli Thayar
significance: A Vishnu temple of about 1.5 acres in Mylapore, Chennai, counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams of the Vaishnava tradition and revered as the birthplace of the Alvar poet-saint Peyalvar. It is administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments board, and its very old temple tank was desilted for the first time in 2016.
story: Lakshmi is said to have come to the hermitage of sage Bhrigu after the churning of the ocean of milk and to have been accepted as his daughter Bhargavi, whom the presiding deity then married; the saint Peyalvar is held to have been found in the temple's Manikairavam well.

name: Chokkeeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Kanchipuram raised by the Cholas in the 9th century CE and also known as the Kousikeswarar temple. It is one of the protected monuments of Tamil Nadu under the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Aazhimala Shiva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on a cliff beside the Arabian Sea near Vizhinjam in southern Kerala, built in a style close to that of Tamil Nadu with a sculpted gopuram. It is known above all for an 18-metre Gangadhareshwara figure carved by the local artist P. S. Devadathan between 2014 and 2020, the tallest Shiva sculpture in Kerala.

name: Sitaleshwar Temple
significance: A 7th-century Shiva shrine in the Chandrabhaga temple group at Jhalrapatan, to which a pillared hall was added in the 10th century; its columns were praised by James Fergusson, who surveyed the ruins in the 19th century. The original shikhara has collapsed and the rebuilt sanctum now carries a flat roof with a small dome; it is a Monument of National Importance (N-RJ-71).

name: Boro Maa Kali Temple, Naihati
significance: A Kali shrine at Naihati begun in 1923 by Bhavesh Chakraborty, a jute-mill worker and social worker, famous for the twenty-two-foot image raised each year at Kali Puja and dressed in some twelve kilograms of gold and two hundred of silver. A permanent temple with a stone image was inaugurated in 2023, and the immersion procession draws crowds large enough to need over a thousand police.
story: Chakraborty is said to have been told by Kali in a dream to shape her as a giant twenty-two-foot image like those he had seen at Nabadwip.

name: Tholung Monastery
deity: Nyingma lineage; relics of Lama Lhatsun Chenpo
significance: A remote Nyingma monastery at about 8,000 feet in Upper Dzongu, inside the buffer zone of Khangchendzonga National Park, first raised under Chogyal Phuntsog Namgyal II and built in its present form in 1789 by Pema Dechhen Gyatso, with the standing structure reconstructed in 1980. It safeguards manuscripts and relics carried here during the Gorkha invasions, shown to the public only once every three years at the Kamsil ceremony in April.
story: The site is held to have been revealed as sacred ground in 1760 by the fourth Lhatsun, Kunzang Jigmed Gyatso.

name: Arunachalesvarar Temple, Ammapettai
significance: A Shiva temple at Ammapettai in Papanasam taluk, about 21 km east of Thanjavur, laid out with a prakara, mahamandapa and kosta niches holding several subsidiary shrines. Its most recent consecration, the Kumbhabhishekam, was performed on 15 September 2005.

name: Shikari Devi Temple
deity: Durga as Shikari Devi (goddess of the hunt)
significance: A roofless stone shrine to Durga on Shikari peak, at 3,332 m the highest point in Mandi district and the centre of the Shikari Devi Sanctuary above the Janjheli and Karsog valleys. Long resorted to by local hunters seeking a good chase, it draws its largest crowds at Navratri.
story: The Pandavas, exiled and hunting here, are said to have chased a deer that vanished into the forest, understood the animal to have been the goddess guiding them, and founded the shrine where they then meditated.

name: Karuvathoor Sreeramaswami Temple
significance: A Rama temple in Velur panchayat, Thrissur district, with a rectangular shrine under a domed and tiled roof and sculpture entirely in the Kerala idiom. Consecrated by the Azhvancheri Thamprakkal and long held by Azhvancheri Mana and later Avanaparambu Mana of Kiralur, it now runs under the Cochin Devaswom Board through the Nelluvai Mullakkal Devaswom.

name: Rankini Temple, Jadugora
place: Rohinibera, Potka block, East Singhbhum district
deity: Rankini, worshipped as a form of Kali
significance: A goddess shrine near Jadugora whose object of worship is a stone taken to be Rankini herself; the present building was put up between 1947 and 1950 after Dinbandhu Singh began the worship, and a family trust has run it since 1954. Originally a Bhumij tribal cult, it saw human sacrifice until the British stopped the practice around 1865.
story: The goddess is said to have taken the form of a girl fleeing a shepherd who hid in a washerman's bundle of clothes at Kapadgadi Ghat, whereupon the pile of cloth turned to stone.

name: Lingdum Monastery
deity: Zurmang Kagyu lineage, seat of Zurmang Gharwang Rinpoche
significance: A modern monastery near Ranka, about an hour from Gangtok, completed in 1999 and also known as Ranka Lingdum or the Pal Zurmang Kagyud Monastery. It belongs to the Zurmang Kagyu tradition of Tibetan Buddhism and is led by Zurmang Gharwang Rinpoche.

name: Mahamaya Temple, Raipur
significance: The goddess temple of Raipur's old quarter, ascribed to Raja Mordhwaj and rebuilt in Nagara style under the Marathas in the 17th–18th centuries, with a second shrine to Samaleswari. It is counted among the thirty-six Shakti pithas of Chhattisgarh and is run by the Shree Rajrajeshwari Maa Mahamaya Devi Mandir Raipur Trust.
story: King Mordhwaj is said to have found the image in the Karun river as a rock ringed by three giant serpents, and the goddess revealed herself to him as his family deity and asked that a temple be raised for her.

name: Kamna Devi Temple
deity: Kamna Devi, a form of Ambika
significance: A goddess temple on Prospect Hill above Boileauganj, one of Shimla's seven hills, at 2,176 m among deodar, pine, oak and rhododendron, with views across southern Shimla to the Tara Devi temple. It is credited to the Rana of Junga in the 18th century, though the exact date of its founding is unknown, and pilgrims come chiefly with family and marriage concerns.

name: Rinchenpong Monastery
significance: The third-oldest monastery in Sikkim, founded in 1730 by the Ngadakpa Lama above the twin villages of Rinchenpong and Kaluk at over 1,700 m, and begun with some ninety-eight lamas. It is a training centre for monks and keeps a rare image of the primordial Adi-Buddha in the Yab-Yum posture, in whose sanctum photography is now barred; the nearby Poison Pokhri lake is remembered as a symbol of resistance to foreign invasion.

name: Kapilnath Temple
significance: A 17th-century Shiva temple near Navratangarh in Gumla district, built in 1643 CE by the Nagvanshi king Ram Shah, successor of Durjan Shah, after the dynasty moved its capital from Khukhragarh. Unusually the Shiva linga stands outside rather than inside the shrine, and the temple draws its largest crowds at Shivratri.
story: Ram Shah is said to have seen his cow's milk dripping into the mouth of a cobra and then to have beheld Shiva himself, and on his guru's advice resolved to build the temple.

name: Tsuklakhang Palace
significance: The royal chapel of the Chogyals of Sikkim at Gangtok, established in 1898, whose altars carry images of the Buddha, bodhisattvas and tantric deities and whose halls hold a large collection of Buddhist scripture. It served as the setting for royal coronations, marriages and victory ceremonies, and hosts the Pang Lhabsol festival in mid-September in honour of Mount Khangchendzonga.

name: Maa Khadgeshwari Kali Mandir
deity: Kali, with Shiva in the same premises
significance: A Kali temple in the town of Araria whose image was first housed in a thatched hut in 1884; work on the present building began in 1987 and finished in 2011, funded by donations and public subscription. At 152 feet it is claimed to be the tallest Kali temple in the world, and it has been managed since the early 1970s by Sarojanand Dixit, a former footballer known as Nanu Baba.

name: Phensang Monastery
significance: A monastery of the Nyingma order about 9 km north of Gangtok, established in 1721 in the time of Jigme Pawo. Its principal festival falls on the 28th and 29th days of the tenth Tibetan month.

name: Ghanteshwar Temple, Mumbai
significance: A Hanuman temple in Khar West, Mumbai, founded in 1960 by a local man, Sakharam Rahate, and busiest on Tuesdays and Saturdays and at Hanuman Jayanti. Its name comes from the great number of bells hung about it.
story: Devotees hold that a wish granted here must be repaid with a bell, which is why the temple has accumulated so many.

name: Ulagalandha Perumal Temple, Singanallur
deity: Ulagalandha Perumal (Vishnu), with Sridevi and Bhoodevi
significance: A Vishnu temple in the Singanallur quarter of Coimbatore whose north-facing presiding image is cast in panchaloha. It was renovated in 2000 and its seven-tiered tower consecrated at a Kumbhabhishekam in 2005.
story: The temple's own account holds that the Chola king Karikalan founded it while passing through Singanallur on a campaign, for the welfare of the people.

name: Bermiok Monastery
deity: Amitābha and the thousand-armed Avalokiteśvara (Karma Kagyu)
significance: A Karma Kagyu monastery above Singtam in southern Sikkim, founded in 1873 and rebuilt in 1954 after earthquake damage. Its manilhakang holds images of Amitabha and the thousand-armed Avalokiteshvara, and its prayer-wheel building, also of 1954, was rebuilt in 1987.
